title: ImProver: Agent-Based Automated Proof Optimization
abstract: ImProver is a large-language-model agent that rewrites proofs to optimize arbitrary user-defined metrics in Lean, such as length or readability. We test ImProver on rewriting real-world undergraduate theorems, competition problems, and research-level mathematics, finding that ImProver is capable of rewriting proofs so that they are substantially shorter, more readable, and more declarative in style.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a complex math problem. You want your solution to be not only correct but also easy to understand and concise. Proof optimization is the process of rewriting a formal proof to meet these criteria. We can think of it like editing a piece of writing to make it clearer and more engaging. In this case, the 'writing' is a formal proof, and the 'editor' is our ImProver system.

By optimizing proofs, we can make them more accessible and useful for both humans and machines.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
ImProver uses a combination of techniques, including Chain-of-States prompting and retrieval, to generate optimized proofs. It works by first analyzing the input proof and identifying areas for improvement. Then, it uses a large language model to generate new proof steps that meet the desired criteria.

The system can be fine-tuned to optimize for different metrics, such as length or readability.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
We evaluated ImProver on several datasets, including Mathematics in Lean (MIL), Compfiles, and Mathlib. The results show that ImProver significantly outperforms the base GPT-4o model in terms of improvement and accuracy. For example, on the MIL dataset, ImProver achieved an average improvement of 30.54% in length and 13.45% in readability, compared to 6.25% and 4.18% for GPT-4o, respectively.

These results demonstrate the effectiveness of ImProver in optimizing proofs for various metrics.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
Optimizing proofs is important because it can make them more accessible and useful for both humans and machines. By generating more readable and concise proofs, we can improve the overall quality of formal mathematics and make it easier to learn and understand.

Additionally, optimized proofs can be used to improve the performance of automated theorem proving systems, which can have significant impacts on fields such as computer science, mathematics, and engineering.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
ImProver introduces several key innovations, including Chain-of-States prompting and retrieval. These techniques allow the system to generate optimized proofs that meet specific criteria, such as length or readability.

The system also uses a large language model to generate new proof steps, which can be fine-tuned to optimize for different metrics.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To try ImProver yourself, you can access the code and datasets on our GitHub repository. You can also experiment with different metrics and optimization techniques to see how they impact the quality of the generated proofs.

We encourage you to explore the possibilities of proof optimization and contribute to the development of ImProver.
